description: A Martian map is more than lines on dust
summary:
ARES is a 3D web app that lets you explore Mars the way Google Earth lets you explore our planet. I built it for the NASA Space Apps Challenge to help astronauts plan a safe spacewalk before they ever step outside.

You can spin a realistic Mars globe made from real NASA and USGS data, visit 17 landing sites, search for craters and mountains, and switch between map layers like elevation, heat, and terrain roughness. It also tracks Mars’s moons and orbiting spacecraft in real time and shows live Martian time.

At the heart of ARES is a 5-step mission planner. You pick a landing site and a science goal, overlay the data layers, and the app finds a safe route that avoids steep slopes and sand. It then checks radiation levels and spacesuit limits, and you can view it all through a helmet-style HUD.

Exploring Mars safely depends on clear, trustworthy maps. ARES brings real planetary data into one simple tool that anyone can use, from students to future crews.
details:
What it does and how it works
ARES is a 3D Mars globe that runs in your web browser, like Google Earth but for Mars. You can zoom around the planet, search for craters and mountains, visit 17 real landing sites, and switch between NASA map layers such as elevation, temperature, and rough terrain. It tracks Mars’s moons and orbiting spacecraft in real time, shows the live Martian time, and has a tool to measure distances across the surface.

The main feature is a 5-step spacewalk planner. You pick a landing site and a science goal, stack the map layers to check the terrain, and ARES finds a safe walking route that avoids steep slopes and sand. It then shows radiation levels and spacesuit limits, and you can view everything through a helmet-style HUD.

Benefits and impact
Astronauts will need clear maps and a way to plan each spacewalk safely. ARES puts real data from several space agencies into one easy tool. It can also help students and the public explore Mars for themselves.

Tools and technology

  • TypeScript, CesiumJS (3D globe), Vite, and Tailwind CSS
  • A small Node.js backend for data
  • Real data from NASA Mars Trek, USGS, and NASA’s Mars24 time algorithms
  • Playwright for automated testing
  • No special hardware needed, just a laptop or phone with a modern browser

What makes it creative

  • It combines a realistic globe, live orbit tracking, route planning, and a helmet view in one app.
  • An AI “super-resolution” feature sharpens the map, with a before/after slider. It also warns users that the sharpened image is synthetic, not real science data.
  • It works smoothly with laptop trackpads and touchscreens.

What we considered

  • Accuracy: I used Mars’s real shape and measured distances along the surface correctly.
  • Readability: The panels are solid and high-contrast so text is easy to read over the globe.
  • Speed: It’s tuned to run smoothly at 60 frames per second.
  • Honesty: The app clearly labels AI-enhanced images so nobody mistakes them for raw data.
